hero.description: Gym Guide is made for people who are new to fitness or want a clear path without feeling lost.

about.body: Our guide is designed to provide you with all the necessary information for the gym. To benefit from it, we highly recommend following these steps.

steps.title: EXPLORE
steps.desc: Check the exercises and splits sections to understand the basic anatomy of the body and how exercising works.

steps.title: SELECT
steps.desc: After understanding basic muscle anatomy and knowing "What is an exercise?" and "What is a split?", choose one of the splits that suits your routine, or try creating one yourself!

steps.title: CONSULT
steps.desc: Ask the AI coach for anything you find confusing. And of course we encourage you to search in other references to know exactly what you are doing in the gym.

tools.body: What you get: explained exercises and workout plans, practical tips, and an AI coach you can ask anything. No complicated stuff – just tools that actually help.

dailyTip.label: Daily Tip
dailyTip.desc: Showing up 4 times a week at 70% effort will always beat a single 100% workout followed by 2 weeks of recovery. Focus on the habit first.

feedback.body: We would be so happy to receive your suggestions, criticisms, or anything you would like to share with us regarding this guide ♥
feedback.quote: "Your feedback is the data that drives our progression. Every report is reviewed for system optimization."

header.body: the exercises you need to build muscle

anatomySection.subTitle: The Science of Hypertrophy
anatomySection.paragraph1: Exercise does a lot for your heart, your mind, and burning fat. But the main focus here is building and growing muscle. (Some exercises aren't meant for muscle growth – but in this guide, we'll talk specifically about muscle‑building.)
anatomySection.paragraph2: Your body has several major muscle groups: chest, shoulders, legs, back, and more – see the map below. Each group can be trained with a certain motion. That motion becomes an exercise when you add tension to the muscle, for example by grabbing some dumbbells while moving.

muscleGroupsSection.subTitle: Targeted Training Protocols
muscleGroupsSection.body: Now here our exercises are divided by muscle groups. Click at any group to see its exercises

header.body: the needed knowledge to create your training routine

steps.title: HOW MANY DAYS
steps.desc: Before anything, answer yourself honestly: how many days can you go to the gym? 1 day? 2 days? 3 days? Or more?

steps.title: CHOOSE A SUITABLE PLAN
steps.desc: If you have 1 day, train full body. If you have 2 days, train upper/lower split. If you have 3 days, train push/pull/legs split, and so on.

steps.title: CHOOSING THE EXERCISES
steps.desc: Choose the exercises for each training session. For example, if the session is chest and triceps: for chest – bench press; for triceps – rope pushdown, etc.

steps.title: PRIORITIZE WEAK MUSCLES
steps.desc: For intermediate and advanced levels, prioritize muscle groups or heads that lag behind. For instance, if your upper chest is weaker, replace a lower chest exercise with an upper chest one.

whatIsSplit.subTitle: One Goal, Multiple Paths
whatIsSplit.paragraph1: First of all, we don't recommend creating your first training split yourself as a complete beginner. But it is preferable to understand how the split is generally created.
whatIsSplit.paragraph2: To create a training split, the first most important question is: how many days can you train a week? And to answer this question you must consider time, food and sleep factors.

selectSplit.subTitle: Deployment Options
selectSplit.body: choose the training split that best suits your schedule and goals.
